cards.title: Protect deep work windows from shallow obligations
cards.insight: Peak productivity occurs when you can concentrate uninterrupted on cognitively demanding tasks, yet most work environments fragment attention into constant context-switching. The cost of resuming focus after interruption multiplies when you have back-to-back meetings, Slack notifications, and reactive email cycles.
cards.takeaway: Block 2-3 hour windows on your calendar for focused work and treat them with the same non-negotiable priority as client meetings.

cards.title: Energy management beats time management
cards.insight: Hours spent tired, distracted, or unmotivated produce far less output than fewer hours spent in a state of full engagement and mental clarity. Your most valuable asset isn't how many hours you work—it's the quality of attention you bring to those hours.
cards.takeaway: Track when you feel most alert and productive over one week, then schedule your hardest thinking work during those peak windows.

cards.title: Single-task mastery builds long-term advantage
cards.insight: Multitasking creates an illusion of productivity while fragmenting the depth needed to produce exceptional work or develop genuine expertise. The ability to sustain focus on one problem until it's solved compounds over months and years into mastery others cannot replicate.
cards.takeaway: Choose one priority per day—not three—and don't move to the next task until that one reaches a natural stopping point.

cards.title: Friction against distraction is your most valuable tool
cards.insight: Willpower is finite, so the most reliable productivity strategy isn't about discipline—it's about making distractions harder to access than focused work. Removing notifications, logging out of social apps, and physically separating from your phone reduces the daily friction of choosing focus.
cards.takeaway: Audit your workspace and devices tomorrow: delete three apps, disable three categories of notifications, and create one physical barrier between you and your phone during work blocks.
